<definition_of_ready maturity="Executable" cumulative="true">

Judge every criterion; this table includes the complete Proposed, Framed, and Sliced requirements and is the complete criterion set for Executable Maturity, so apply no criterion outside it. Each criterion judges the record against the record rule it names in `<record_rules>`.

| ID                          | Criterion                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `executable-record`         | The front matter and the body's section set and order satisfy `record-shape`, the title and Intent satisfy `record-limits`, and the body opens with `## Intent`.                                                                                                                |
| `executable-identity`       | `title`, `product`, `maturity: Executable`, and `lifecycle` identify one intended Output, its owning Product or none for a root, and a valid Lifecycle under `record-shape`.                                                                                                    |
| `executable-relationships`  | `refined_from`, `parent`, and `blocked_by` satisfy `lineage` and `blockers`, `blocked_by` names every known blocker, and the dependency graph has no blocker cycle.                                                                                                             |
| `executable-intent`         | `## Intent` states What, Why, and Evidence under `intent`, with Observation present only where an observation gives rise to the Change.                                                                                                                                         |
| `executable-input-boundary` | The record satisfies `received-input-boundary`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `executable-body-authority` | The body satisfies `body-authority`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `executable-governance`     | For a Leaf, `## Governance` lists every governing record with its verdict `in line`, `amended`, or `new` under `governance`.                                                                                                                                                    |
| `executable-mutations`      | For a Leaf, the Governance mutations and Spec mutations blocks state every consequential decision for the changeset under `governance-mutations` and `spec-mutations`, in an execution order that lets the Executor proceed without reopening product or architecture judgment. |
| `executable-open-questions` | `## Open questions` is empty or absent under `open-questions`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `executable-slice`          | A Leaf's `## Slice` names the one repository and the one observable check of one coherent, independently integrable unit whose dependencies and sequence are resolved, under `slice`; a Parent never reaches Executable, under `change-type`.                                   |
| `executable-artifacts`      | Every link in `## Artifacts` names a record or Node of the mutations blocks and pins the commit that holds its audited content, under `artifacts`; an empty section satisfies the criterion.                                                                                    |

</definition_of_ready>

<merge_composition>

Execution applies this composition to derive each block's results and Verifiers; the record names none. It operationalizes the `Merge` section of the Projection chapter, `versions/4.0/methodology/product-tree/verification/projection.md` inside the declared `methodology.source`.

- Touch: a changeset touches a node directly through its spec, its status claim, a decision record or outcome record the node holds, a verification artifact under its `tests/`, `evals/`, or `probes/`, a file its linked verification reaches, or a file one of its `[audit]` assertions names as its subject. It touches a node through a dependency through a decision record that governs the node, or a path a result pin in the node's status claim reads.
- Selected predicates: every changeset selects Validate and the coverage predicate — every changed implementation file is reached by some node's linked verification — with the attested probe results the status claims carry. A least malleable target of `spec` adds no agentic predicate. A least malleable target of `verification` adds Review. A least malleable target of `implementation` adds the evidence audits and Review, with the evidence audits run before Review. The evidence audits cover each touched node that is itself `implementation`-malleable and whose evidence result is missing or invalidated, a change to the implementation its linked verification reaches included; a `spec`- or `verification`-malleable node takes no evidence audit, whatever code sits under it. A node's evidence result is its status claim's passed evidence entry, pinned to the node's spec, its `tests/` or `evals/` directory, and the implementation files its linked verification reaches; a node with no such entry has a missing result. A node whose `[test]` result is missing or invalidated takes the test-evidence audit, and one whose `[eval]` result is missing or invalidated takes the eval-evidence audit. A product spec or outcome-record change adds Review whatever the least malleable target. The `spec-mutations` record rule states the malleability order.
- Results: a changeset that changes a pinned path invalidates that result; a node's Audit results stay valid only when every pinned change is a link-format edit. A node whose declarations are unchanged and that reached `Passing` produces each invalidated result again before merge. A node that never reached `Passing` derives `Declared` or `Specified` until every result its malleability requires is current and passes. A node whose declarations change merges in the state it derives, unless dependency protection fails the changeset because it raises a malleability or ends `Passing` in the closure of an effectively `Passing` consumer; execution then produces each result still missing, and the Change reaches `Applied` only when no Node of the Spec mutations is failing.
- Producers by kind: the test runner for `[test]`, the eval harness for `[eval]`, the Author's attested run for `[probe]`, and the configured audit Verifier for `[audit]`. A result whose producer the repository does not ship names the Change that supplies it as a blocker.
- Authoring checks: each added or changed decision record receives its decision-record audit before merge, at any malleability, and that audit produces no node-local result.

</merge_composition>
